capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor skill, invoked with bank details from the chosen quote

inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders

instructions.note: The only safeguard on payment destination is the instruction 'only pay vendors on the approved list' plus 'use the bank details from the chosen quote.' Nothing structural binds the paid bank details to a verified record for that vendor, so an approved-list match on name alone does not prevent a bank-detail swap in a spoofed quote.

'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' assumes a downstream safety net. Runtime notes contradict this: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no further checks.

elements.name: Manager approval record (item and budget, pre-quote)

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: The gate itself does not weaken with model capability, but it approves item and budget before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent. It never constrains vendor selection or bank details, so it earns no credit against cap.delegate_payment; it gates a different decision than the one that is exploited.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to only pay approved vendors
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends on the model matching vendor identity against the approved list; it does not verify that the bank details supplied in a quote match records tied to that vendor. A spoofed quote impersonating an already-approved vendor with swapped bank details satisfies this check on name alone. A more capable model subjected to a convincing spoofed quote is equally, if not more, likely to accept the match.

controls.name: Static bearer token authentication between orchestrator and payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: The token authorizes the caller, not the task content or the destination identity. payments-agent accepts any task carrying the token and performs no independent validation, so this control neither constrains payment content nor prevents endpoint spoofing; it earns no credit against either finding.

controls.name: Bind payment bank details to a verified vendor master record
controls.decay_rationale: Would make quote-supplied bank details insufficient on their own to authorize payment, severing the authority-laundering path.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval at payment execution, with approval context propagated to payments-agent
Signed and pinned agent card with mutual authentication for payments-agent

findings.title: Lethal trifecta / authority laundering (TC1+TC7): untrusted vendor quote drives irreversible payment despite an approved-vendor check and a manager approval that covers a different decision

attack_path.note: Untrusted external vendor email/attachment carries attacker-controlled bank details.
Only the vendor name is checked against the approved list; bank details are not verified against any record.
Manager approved item and budget before this quote existed; approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
Orchestrator delegates a payment task to payments-agent using bank details taken directly from the chosen quote.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no further checks.

forecast.watch_signal: A model or version change in subject.model, removal or softening of the 'only pay vendors on the approved list' prompt line, or rising median steps/runtime per purchase task without added bank-detail verification controls.

evidence.observation: Orchestrator is instructed to choose the best quote and hand it to payments-agent to pay, using 'the bank details from the chosen quote,' directly trusting untrusted quote content for payment execution.
Manager approves item and budget before any quote exists; the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so approval does not constrain vendor or bank-detail selection.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no further checks.

recommendations.action: Verify payment bank details against a vendor master record maintained independently of inbound quotes; reject or hold payments where bank details differ from the record on file.

Add a raw-action human approval gate immediately before payment execution that shows the approver the selected vendor, amount, and bank details, and propagate that approval context to payments-agent for independent validation.
Have payments-agent independently validate vendor identity and amount against its own authorization record rather than trusting bearer-token-authenticated task content alone.
Log and alert whenever a payment's bank details differ from the last payment made to the same vendor.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card enables peer impersonation / rug-pull redefinition of the payment destination (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup, not signed or pinned; peer identity is not verified (peer_identity_verified: false).
Orchestrator delegates the payment task, including bank details, to whatever endpoint currently resolves as payments-agent; a spoofed or rug-pulled endpoint receives full payment authority.

forecast.watch_signal: Addition of further A2A peers without signed/pinned agent cards and mutual authentication; any unexplained DNS, certificate, or endpoint change for payments.internal.example.

evidence.observation: Authentication scheme is a bare bearer token; no signature or identity binding is described.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card; verify the signature and pin on every fetch, not only at startup.
Use mutual TLS or signed identity assertions for the A2A channel instead of a static bearer token.
Alert on any change to payments-agent's resolved endpoint, certificate, or skill definitions.

rating.rationale: Two independent critical-severity paths reach an irreversible, confidential payment capability (cap.delegate_payment). Finding 1 (authority laundering): an untrusted vendor quote supplies bank details directly into payment, the only preventive control is a behavioral, model-dependent approved-vendor instruction, and the one human approval gate covers a different decision (item and budget, approved before the quote exists, record not propagated), so it earns no credit; residual lands at high and collapses to critical the moment the vendor-allowlist instruction fails (model_upgrade, control_removal, or longer_task_horizon). Finding 2 (peer impersonation): the A2A connection to payments-agent has no signed/pinned identity, so residual is already critical with no mitigating control. Overall residual and forecast are both critical; the single highest-leverage fix is binding payment bank details to a verified vendor record and propagating approval context to payments-agent (ctl.bank_detail_verification, ctl.payment_execution_approval), alongside signing/pinning the payments-agent card.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or JSON schema for cap.delegate_payment or cap.vendor_list_read was provided; capability scope and argument structure are inferred from the system prompt, agent card, and runtime notes, at medium confidence.
max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not specified in the provided artifacts; both were treated as null, which triggers the rubric's autonomy modifier for S2/S3 sinks.

No evidence was available on whether network position or DNS/TLS control would be required to exploit the unsigned/unpinned payments-agent card; Finding 2's confidence is set to medium to reflect that gap.
